items.title: Frank Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 7, 1998
items.q: Now see the Sinatras, the Joe Williams, Sarah Vaughan, Ella Fitzgerald, Tony Bennett, they have jazz singer mentalities.

ctx.x: Eleven years, wow. And you had mentioned Sinatra, and thinking about vocalists, did the guys in the band ever kind of resent the vocalist being out front and doing four or five songs a night and was that something that you guys felt like you didn’t feel it was necessary?

Well the professionalism in this particular orchestra didn’t allow for that kind of attitude on a large scale. And we loved Sinatra, we loved Billy Eckstine, we loved Sarah Vaughan and we loved Tony Bennett, and there just was no feeling of that kind. Whenever we knew we were going to work with them we said well we’re going to have some fun now. Some others, who shall remain nameless, we didn’t have as much fun with because some of them didn’t have the quality arrangements that we would like to play, and some of…
Well you certainly had a powerhouse band there for those years, plus with Joe Williams on board, and a great time. Fortunately you recorded a lot so it’s documented.

items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: Did he like jazz, Jerry Lewis?

Loved it. He came to see us at Birdland. He would insist on directing the band on Apri in Paris or something. And other income. We recorded with Sarah Vaughan. We recorded with Nat “King” Cole. We recorded with Ella Fitzgerald. We recorded with -- I don’t think Lena Horne came ’til later. Frank Sinatra of course came -- that was later in the ’60s, but these recordings paid well as well.
So this is adding -- then there’s your work totally outside of that domain.
